Hi Alice — great to connect yesterday. As promised, I put together a short, pragmatic comparison of the two procurement lanes so your finance and procurement teams can weigh timing, invoicing, tax, and co-sell implications. High-level options: 

1) Cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure private offer)
- Pros: Fast procurement for pilots (private offer), predictable SKU-based billing, potential credits from marketplace co-sell programs, single-pane subscription for infra teams.
- Cons: Longer payout cadence for reseller/co-sell credit recognition, some marketplaces require a reseller/private-offer flow that changes invoice party.

2) Direct enterprise PO (invoice to Redwood, signed MSA)
- Pros: Straightforward invoicing to your AP, easier for custom SOW terms, faster recognition of revenue on our side which helps tailored discounts.
- Cons: Adds PO/contract admin on both sides; may take longer if legal redlines are heavy.

Ask: can you share the procurement team's preferred lane and any internal constraints (e.g., must be on marketplace to get cloud credits, payment net terms required, or tax/residency needs)? I attached a simple ROI workbook that maps estimated token usage for the pilot.

Attachments: FinWave_MRP_ROI.xlsx (excel)

If you like, Kimberly can outline what a 30-day pilot looks like under each lane and I can draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) for approvals.

Best,
Vanessa

Hi Alice — quick answers to your procurement questions and tradeoffs below. I also attached a short one-pager (cheat sheet) that teams find useful when drafting MAPs. 

1) Seller of record / invoicing
- Marketplace private offer: Seller of record depends on the marketplace and listing model. For AWS private offers we can be seller of record or route via AWS depending on the private offer configuration — we typically choose "Redwood as seller" for easier support and to avoid reseller VAT complexity. We'll confirm on a case-by-case basis.

2) Co-sell & credits
- Co-sell eligibility does not change the customer's billing rate. Credits/incentives are typically paid out to the vendor partner as market incentives and do not reduce the invoice line for the customer. If there is a joint promotional credit, we can document that in the MAP.

3) Typical timelines
- Marketplace private offer: 3–10 business days if legal and PO are minimal (private offer + minimal acceptance).
- Direct enterprise PO + MSA: 7–30 business days depending on redlines; faster if you accept our standard MSA and we exchange a PO.

4) Compliance artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II report: available upon NDA; we can share a redacted report through our secure portal.
- Data retention and logging: short PDF we maintain for pilots; happy to summarize.

Recommendation based on your goals (board timeline + pilot size ~$20k/month): pursue an AWS private offer for speed, but prepare a signature-ready MSA in parallel so legal can sign the MSA quickly if redlines occur. That hedges risk and preserves AP preferences.

Doc: redwood_marketplace_cheat_sheet.pdf (attached)
DocuSign draft for MSA: https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-for-finwave-msa

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call with your procurement and legal to walk through the private offer flow.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
